blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario S2, code generation with Claude Code. A team uses Claude Code for refactoring and tests. A skill explains how an old billing system works, and Claude should consult it when relevant, while typing its name would do nothing useful. Which header line fits?

options.says: Ruled out because it does the opposite, so that only the person starts it and "the full skill loads only when you invoke it".
Ruled out because a pre-approval for git commands says nothing about who may start the skill, since the field "Pre-approves the listed tools for the turn that invokes the skill".
It hides the skill from the person and leaves it available to Claude, which suits background knowledge.
Ruled out because "The subagent doesn't see your conversation history", so a fork would run a background note as a task with nothing to do.

questions.stem: Scenario S2, code generation with Claude Code. A team uses Claude Code for refactoring and tests. The team's review skill must be unable to change files for the turn that runs it. Which header line does that?

options.says: Ruled out because the pre-approval field "does not restrict which tools are available".
A bare name in the removal field takes the tool out of the pool while the skill is active.
Ruled out because `argument-hint` "only shows the expected shape in autocomplete".
Ruled out because "only a bare name removes a tool", so the scoped entry leaves editing in place.

origin.section: Tools, arguments, forked skills and the practice

questions.stem: Scenario S2, code generation with Claude Code. A team uses Claude Code for refactoring and tests. A command text reads 'Summarise the commits by $ARGUMENTS since yesterday', and a developer runs `/standup ana`. What does Claude receive?

options.text: The sentence unchanged, with the name in a separate note
options.says: Ruled out because the placeholder takes "All arguments, as typed" and is replaced in the text.

options.text: The sentence with a blank where the name belongs
options.says: Ruled out because a blank arises only for a named placeholder without an argument, since an indexed one "stays in the content unchanged", and here the input is given.

options.text: The sentence with the name filled in and a line `ARGUMENTS: ana` after it
options.says: Ruled out because the extra line appears only when "no placeholder receives them", and this one did.

options.text: The sentence with the name filled in and nothing appended
options.says: The placeholder received the input, so it is substituted and nothing is added.
